transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-07
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Cerulean Head of ML), Priya Raman (Cerulean Platform), Samir Patel (CFO - joined 32:00)

Summary (auto): quick scoping for PoC focused on cost modelling, unit economics, and benchmarks.

00:00 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making the time. I'm Maya, AE on the account, with Diego from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
00:12 - Jordan Lee: Good thanks. Appreciate it. We're excited to scope this out — we want to validate cost before we commit to a full rollout.
00:25 - Diego Alvarez: Cool. Quick agenda: success criteria, traffic shape/size, bench plan, per-token estimates for hosted vs dedicated, batching/caching knobs, timeline. We'll capture next steps.
01:03 - Priya Raman: Quick intro from our side — me+Jordan are running platform + ML; Samir may hop on for budgeting later in the call. Our initial ask: conversational recommender across web + in-store kiosks, about 200 reqs/sec peak expected during sales, average session 3-4 turns.
01:45 - Jordan: To be concrete, typical prompt sizes are 80-120 tokens input, and expected output ~250 tokens. We also have a lot of repeated prefixes — product descriptions reuse the same catalog context.
02:05 - Diego: That's helpful. So ballpark tokens per request: inputs 100 + outputs 250 = 350 tokens. With 200 req/s peak, that's 70k tokens/sec peak, which is pretty high. We'll sketch both 200 rps peak and a 24-hour average.
02:30 - Maya: One of the key questions — success criteria. Jordan, what are your KPIs? Latency? Quality? Cost?
02:45 - Jordan: Latency SLO is 95th < 300ms for web, <400ms for kiosk. Quality target: model should match our current baseline (in-house tuned LLM) on intent accuracy >= 95% on a test set of 500 prompts. Cost target: need to stay under $X/month — Samir will define the actual number.
03:10 - Diego: Ok, for cost modeling we usually create a per-token scenario: hosted (standard API) using a large open model, versus dedicated reserved capacity with quantized 8-bit runtimes, and private deployment if data residency needed. Each has tradeoffs.
03:40 - Jordan: Can you share sample per-token numbers? Even roughs help us understand magnitude.
03:55 - Diego: Sure. Rough estimates (very rough, ballpark): hosted (latest 13B-ish variant) generation cost ~ $0.0006 per token for output and $0.00015 per token for input — so ~ $0.00075 total per token touched. Dedicated quantized / Dedicated reserved capacity running on our optimized runtime can reduce unit cost by ~3-4x — so effective per-token compute cost might be ~ $0.0002. But the dedicated model includes fixed monthly VM/GPU commit (e.g., $20k-$40k/month depending on throughput). These numbers are illustrative and we'll detail them in the spreadsheet.
05:00 - Jordan: Hmm, at 350 tokens/request * 200 rps * 3600s that's... big.
05:15 - Maya: Right, that raw calc is why batching and caching matter. If we can cache the product catalog prefix and only send deltas, the average tokens per request could drop by 30-50% depending on cache hit rate. Also batching across similar short requests can increase GPU utilization and reduce per-token latency/cost amortization.
06:00 - Priya: Our infra team wants to know latency tradeoffs with batching. We can't accept tail latencies >500ms for kiosks.
06:18 - Diego: Understood. There are two knobs: batch size and batch timeout. For interactive SLOs we keep small batch sizes (2-8) and low timeouts (10-50ms), which preserves P95; for background tasks you can push bigger batches. With our runtime, you often see 20-40% cost reduction with small batching when utilization is steady, and up to 2x-3x when you use aggressive batching for high throughput non-interactive flows.
07:05 - Jordan: And caching? What is KV cache vs prefix cache in your platform?
07:20 - Diego: Good question — prefix caching stores repeated prompt prefixes (e.g., product catalog) and we only send delta tokens; KV cache reuses key/value attention states for incremental generation in chat. Both reduce tokens sent to model and also reduce server work. In practice customers with high prefix repetition get 30-60% token savings. We'll want to instrument actual hit-rate for your traffic.
08:00 - Maya: Let's go through a sample scenario: 350 tokens baseline -> with 40% prefix/cache savings -> 210 tokens effective per request. At 200 rps that's 42k tokens/sec. Multiply by 3600 -> 151.2M tokens/hour -> huge. We'll quantify monthly cost in the sheet.
09:05 - Jordan: That monthly math is what's scaring our CFO, Samir.
09:12 - (laughter)
09:20 - Priya: Also we need to consider model size/quality: smaller quantized 7B may be cheaper but might not meet the 95% quality bar. We may need to do A/B or regression testing.
09:40 - Diego: Exactly — part of the PoC will be a quality vs cost sweep: run same prompt set on 7B quant, 13B quant, and a hosted larger model; measure accuracy, latency, and token costs. We'll run bench with your prompts.
10:05 - Maya: Timeline: propose a 3-week PoC: week 1 sample data + config, week 2 bench runs and optimization, week 3 evaluation + exec recap. Is that feasible?
10:25 - Jordan: Yes. We can share sample prompts and traffic shape this week. Prefer bench run next week.
10:35 - Diego: For the benchmark we'll need: sample prompt set (~5k), seq len distribution, target concurrency patterns, and the acceptance criteria. We'll also need to pick exact models to test and the quantization profiles.
11:00 - Priya: On infra — do you support private VPC deployment? We have PII concerns and regional constraints for EU traffic.
11:12 - Maya: Yes — Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem options; we also integrate KMS for key management and provide audit logs. We'll include the SOC2 and whitepaper in the doc share.
11:30 - Jordan: Good. Also curious about burst handling. We sometimes have spikes 2x baseline. How does dedicated vs hosted handle that?
11:45 - Diego: Hosted can autoscale but subject to cold start/queueing depending on capacity; Dedicated can have burst pools configured or autoscaling policies with buffer — there's a cost tradeoff (you pay for buffer reserved capacity or accept degraded latency during spikes). We'll model both.
12:15 - Samir (joined): Hey — sorry for being late. I caught the tail about spikes and cost. Quick question: what's the expected monthly TCO for your raw numbers?
12:30 - Maya: We don't have finalized TCO in-call, but shared roughs: for your steady-state with caching and batching assumed, hosted might be $X-$Yk/month and Dedicated with a mid-size commit might be $20-40k/month plus lower per-token variable. We'll send detailed scenarios.
13:00 - Jordan: Can you show a concrete example on the call?
13:10 - Diego: Sure. Example scenario A (hosted): 350 effective tokens/request -> 200 rps peak -> assume 30% cache hit -> net 245 tokens/request average over day -> monthly tokens (peak math approximated) ~ 500B tokens/month (example) -> at $0.00075/token that's $375k/month. Scenario B (dedicated): with optimized quant and caching, effective token cost ~ $0.0002 and fixed commit $30k -> same token volume -> variable ~ $100k + $30k commit = $130k/month. Big difference. These numbers are estimates; we'll run precise calcs.
15:05 - Jordan: That's helpful; the order-of-magnitude delta is what we need.
15:20 - Priya: Regarding cache hit rates: our catalog is fairly static during day but changes nightly. We should be able to hit 50% for many flows.
15:35 - Diego: Perfect; 50% makes a big difference. We'll model 30/50/70% cases in the spreadsheet.
16:00 - Maya: Quality checks — how will we measure model parity? We propose to run the 500-item test suite and an NLU intent/slot accuracy check plus blind human eval for top-k responses. We'll report accuracy delta and regressions.
16:30 - Jordan: Fine. Also want to instrument token-level cost per route — e.g., search-rewrite vs chat vs embeddings.
16:45 - Diego: We can provide per-route dashboards; Redwood Console supports token-level breakdown and per-model cost. We'll provision a demo dashboard for you.
17:05 - Maya: One more detail — does Redwood provide automatic suggestions for batching/caching config?
17:15 - Diego: Yes, Redwood Optimize recommends batching windows, cache TTLs, and quantization profiles based on workload. It will suggest knobs to hit your cost/latency targets. We'll show that in week 2 tuning.
18:00 - Priya: Security docs please — we need SOC2, data flow diagrams, and isolation details.
18:10 - Maya: We'll share SOC2 report and a whitepaper, plus a short network diagram for Private deployment.
18:30 - Jordan: Ok wrapping up — recap next steps: Maya sends cost model sheet; Diego bench scripts; Jordan shares prompts; Priya shares infra; Samir to set budget. Schedule benchmark for Dec 15.
18:55 - Samir: Sounds good. If the dedicated path gets close to half the hosted spend, I'm supportive pending quality.
19:10 - Maya: Great. We'll follow up with calendar invite and docs. Thanks everyone.
19:20 - (end)

References: redwood-cost-model.xlsx (link shared), benchmark-config.yaml, SOC2_whitepaper.pdf (links in chat).

Notes on transcript: transcription has minor recognition errors (product names sometimes mis-typed), speaker overlap minimal.
